structure.heading: Credit Facility Utilisation, FX Exposure, and Liquidity Stress Scenarios (Q3 2026)
text_content: **Credit Facility Utilisation, FX Exposure, and Liquidity Stress Scenarios (Q3 2026)**

The syndicated revolving credit facility totals USD 300.0m, of which USD 120.0m is drawn as of 30 Jun 2026, representing 40.0% utilisation of committed lines. Availability under the facility therefore stands at USD 180.0m, subject to customary borrowing base mechanics and covenants monitored monthly by the agent bank. No covenant breaches were reported at quarter end; however, acquisition financing commitments and seasonal working capital will be reassessed in July and August 2026 to preserve headroom. Planned undrawn availability supports near-term liquidity and provides access to funding if market conditions tighten.

Net FX exposure for Q3 2026 is concentrated in euros, with a reported position of EUR -45.0m (payables greater than receivables). This short EUR stance creates transaction risk ahead of key payment dates in July–September 2026; as such, the treasury will monitor exposures daily and implement tactical forward cover and option structures where cost-effective. FX risk metrics will be reviewed at the weekly treasury desk call and reported to the CFO on 01 Aug 2026. Counterparty concentrations are limited to top-tier banks, disclosed in the weekly treasury pack.

Stress-testing for Q3 2026 evaluated operational delays, funding market dislocation, and combined shocks through 30 Sep 2026. The 'Customer Delay + FX Shock' scenario results in minimum liquidity headroom of USD 22.0m on 25 Sep 2026. Contingency actions include acceleration of collections, suspension of discretionary capital spending, negotiation of extended supplier payment terms, targeted FX hedging, and activation of bilateral short-term lines with core banks. Responsibility for execution: treasury to implement collections and hedges immediately within 48–72 hours; finance to approve discretionary spend changes within five business days.

structure.heading: Quarter-Ahead Cash Position and Short-Term Funding Plan (Q3 2026)
text_content: **Quarter-Ahead Cash Position and Short-Term Funding Plan (Q3 2026)**

As of 30 June 2026 the consolidated cash and cash equivalents balance stands at USD 182.4m. Treasury maintains these deposits in a mix of demand accounts, overnight money market funds, and short-term time deposits with primary banking counterparties to preserve liquidity and yield. This position funds operating needs, near-term vendor settlements, and scheduled payroll; it also supports planned short-term issuance under the commercial paper program. Treasury policy requires daily cash reporting to the CFO and a weekly liquidity dashboard for the Executive Committee. Given current cash balances, no immediate draw on long-term capital markets is planned during July.

Projected cash flow modelling indicates a minimum cash balance of USD 74.0m on 18 August 2026, driven by scheduled vendor disbursements, seasonal working-capital outflows, and timing of receivables. This represents a 59.4% reduction from the 30 June 2026 balance and informs the quarter-ahead funding posture. Treasury will run daily cash reforecasts, enforce accelerated collection initiatives, and defer non-essential discretionary spend to mitigate downside. Near-term actions include targeted AR collection outreach, weekly capex approvals with business units, and intercompany short-term funding where permissible under governance limits. These measures are designed to preserve operational continuity through mid-August. Monitoring will be escalated to the CFO and weekly liquidity reviews presented to Executive Committee.

The short-term funding plan relies primarily on the commercial paper program, and planned commercial paper outstanding peaks at USD 60.0m on 31 Aug 2026. Issuance will target predominantly USD-denominated, unsecured CP with tenors up to 90 days, distributed across primary dealers to maintain investor diversity and minimise rollover risk. Proceeds will be used to smooth intra-quarter timing gaps and to partially replenish the cash buffer following mid-August outflows. Roadshows with core investors are scheduled in late July to support the August issuance window; legal and operational readiness (dealer agreements, DVP settlement tests) will be completed by 25 July. Contingency measures include accelerated billable receivables collection and monetisation of short-term investments.
